introduction: The Mathematics SBA is a project that allows students to apply mathematical concepts to real-life situations. It contributes 20% to the final CSEC grade.

tasks.title: Project Title
tasks.explanation: The title should be clear and concise, reflecting the focus of the study.

tasks.title: Introduction
tasks.explanation: Provide a background of the study and state the purpose clearly.

tasks.title: Method of Data Collection
tasks.explanation: Describe how you collected your data (e.g., questionnaire, observation).

tasks.title: Presentation of Data
tasks.explanation: Use tables, charts, and graphs to represent the collected data.

tasks.title: Analysis of Data
tasks.explanation: Perform calculations and explain the mathematical relationships found.

tasks.title: Discussion of Findings
tasks.explanation: Interpret the results in the context of your original objective.

tasks.title: Conclusion
tasks.explanation: Summarize the findings and state if the objective was met.

tasks.title: Overall Presentation
tasks.explanation: Organization, grammar, and proper use of mathematical language.

sampleTitle: A study of the spending habits of Grade 10 students at Excellence Secondary School.

sample.body: The purpose of this study is to investigate how Grade 10 students at Excellence Secondary School spend their weekly allowance. Many students often complain about not having enough money, and this study aims to see if the money is being spent wisely on school-related items or other activities.
sample.tips: Make sure your objective is measurable.

sample.body: A questionnaire was designed with 5 questions regarding allowance and spending. This questionnaire was distributed to 30 students in Grade 10 using random sampling.
sample.tips: Specify your sample size and sampling method.

sample.body:
Table 1: Weekly Spending Categories
Category | Amount ($)
Food | 150
Transport | 100
Entertainment | 50
Savings | 20
Total | 320
sample.tips: Label all tables and graphs clearly.

marking: Marks are awarded for the clarity of the objective, the accuracy of data representation, the depth of analysis, and the overall logical flow of the project.
checklist: At least two different types of data presentation (e.g., table and bar chart)
